🌟 linux-android | Shell
🎯 Primary Use Case: Repurposing old Android phones into functional Linux desktops or smart home servers.
✨ Key Features: • Turn Android phone into Linux desktop • Turn Android phone into Home Assistant server • No root required • No PC required • No cloud required
📖 Summary: This repository allows users to transform an old Android phone into a functional Linux desktop environment (like XFCE4, KDE Plasma) or a self-hosted Home Assistant server. It achieves this without requiring root access or a separate PC, leveraging Termux and Termux-X11 for a GPU-accelerated experience.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 homelab-hub | Svelte
🎯 Primary Use Case: Centralized management and visualization of home lab infrastructure components.
✨ Key Features: • Inventory Management (hardware, VMs, apps, storage, networks) • Shares Management (NFS, SMB, iSCSI, etc.) • Export/Import functionality • Interactive Network Visualization (Cytoscape.js) • Hierarchical Tree View
📖 Summary: Home Lab Hub is a self-hosted web application designed to manage and visualize your home lab infrastructure. It provides a centralized platform to track hardware, virtual machines, applications, storage, networks, and their relationships, with features like interactive network visualization and markdown-based documentation.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 KeyForge3D | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Generating 3D printable STL files of keys from photographs for replication.
✨ Key Features: • Key Shape Extraction from photo • Bitting Pattern Analysis • 3D Model Generation • STL File Export • User-Friendly GUI (Tkinter)
📖 Summary: KeyForge3D is a Python application that converts a photograph of a physical key into a 3D-printable STL file. It uses image processing to analyze the key's bitting pattern and generate an accurate 3D model, making it useful for locksmiths and hobbyists for key replication.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 Mailspring | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: A desktop email client that provides a fast, efficient, and extensible way to manage email across multiple accounts on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
✨ Key Features: • Unified Inbox • Snooze • Send Later • Mail Rules • Templates
📖 Summary: Mailspring is a fast, open-source email client for Windows, macOS, and Linux, built with TypeScript, Electron, and React. It features a C++ sync engine for improved performance and reduced resource usage compared to its predecessor, Nylas Mail. The client offers a plugin architecture for extensibility and includes features like a unified inbox, snooze, send later, and mail rules.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ OSS-DocumentScanner | C++
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a mobile application for easily scanning, digitizing, and managing physical documents on their Android devices.
✨ Key Features: • Document scanning and capture • Image enhancement for clarity • PDF conversion • Document organization
📖 Summary: OSS DocumentScanner is an Android application designed for efficient document scanning and management. It leverages advanced image processing techniques to capture, enhance, and organize documents, converting them into digital formats like PDFs.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
